notes: Spec asserts: state stays working through the queued-message arrival, no →ready flicker, the cycle still ends at ready. The recipe asks muse to count slowly with a sleep-based tool call after each number (so the working span is long enough to type into); the driver then sends a second message mid-turn via a plain send step. Live probe (throwaway cwd, tmux) confirmed muse's runtime delivers the mid-turn message via an active_run_delivery into the SAME run (one ("run","started") and one ("run","terminal") span both messages) rather than opening a new turn — so the queued_window phase's no-flicker invariant is a structural guarantee of muse's run lifecycle, not a coincidence of timing. The queued message's own text is not expected to surface anywhere in events.jsonl (runtime.user_intent.* and inbox_item_queued/drained are parser Skip=true) — the spec does not assert it. CORRECTED pre-record: turn_start/queued_window/turn_end were unpinned in the assessed spec (no same_session_as); confirmed against tools/onboarding-factory/internal/validate/expected.go (findMatchingEvent/eventSatisfiesPhase) that an unpinned phase scans ALL session_ids with no implicit fallback to session_birth's session, so a goal-reminder/verify-reminder subagent's own ready-skipping working arc (#1960 shared-context fact 2, live-fixed already in 2-2_auto-executed-tool-call and 2-16_oversized-transcript-line) could vacuously satisfy turn_start/queued_window/turn_end instead of the parent session. Pinned all three to session_birth before driving.

text: Session appears in ready (single-birth: session id is the transcript's parent directory name)
